sentences.text: This appeal by the appellant/driver and owner u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 08.05.2015 passed by Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (in short "Claims Tribunal") Pichhore, Shivpuri in Claim Case No40/2013 whereby Claims Tribunal found breach of terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy and exonerated Insurance Company from liability to pay compensation.

entities.text: Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2 . The date of accident and the finding of negligence are not in dispute.
The controversy in the present appeal relates to the finding of breach of policy conditions and consequential liability NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4745 2 MA-879-2015 3.

As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Anjo in motor accident, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.2,25,000/- has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal with interest from filing of claim petition till its realization.
4. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, learned counsel for the appellants submitted that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in awarding compensation.

It is further submitted this claim petition filed by claimants under SEction 163-A of the MV Act, but Claims Tribunal awarded Ranasingh vs Kishorilal on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18000650/
1 compensation not according to the Second Scheduel of Section 163-A of the MV Act.

Claims Tribunal awaded compensation on the basis of the Apex Court verdict in Sarla Verma learned Claims Tribunal has committed a manifest error of law in holding that the driver was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident.
The evidence on record establishes that driver was duly licensed to drive a motorbike and tractor, which entitled him to drive the vehicle in question.
The finding to the contrary is erroneous and contrary to settled law.

It is further submitted that the finding of violation of policy conditions on the ground of absence of permit and fitness certificate is unsustainable, as no evidence from any competent officer of the Transport Department was adduced to prove such alleged violation.

Mere non-production of documents cannot, by itself,
establish breach of policy conditions.

Moreover, the vehicle owned by appellant No.2, though insured as a commercial vehicle, was being used for private purposes at the relevant time, for which no permit or fitness certificate was required.
Therefore, the conclusion drawn by the learned NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4745 3 MA-879-2015 Tribunal regarding breach of policy conditions is illegal and deserves to be set aside.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents opposed the misc. appeal and prayed for rejection of the same.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
On perusal of the record as well as paragraph 9 of the impugned award, it is clear that at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle was not having a valid permit and fitness certificate.
The appellants failed to adduce any documentary or oral evidence to establish the existence of a valid permit or fitness certificate at the relevant time.
Thus, there was a clear breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Consequently, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation amount to the claimants.

8. At this stage, the appellants have sought a "pay and recover"
order, requesting that the Insurance Company pay the compensation and subsequently recover the amount from them.
However, this Court observed that the purpose of a "pay and recover" order is to prevent undue harassment of the claimants in recovering compensation.
In the present case, where the appellants have admitted the breach of insurance policy terms, the Court finds no reason to invoke the "pay and recover" mechanism.
The object underlying this principle is to avoid multiplicity of proceedings, which would only cause inconvenience to the claimants and would not serve the interests of justice in this case.

[also See: Siyaram and Others vs.
Shankar and Others decided on 28th of August, 2025 in Misc. Appeal No. 408 of 2012].

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4745 4 MA-879-2015 9.
In light of the above findings, the Miscellaneous Appeal filed by the appellants is dismissed.
The compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal stands affirmed.

The appellants (owner and driver of Ranasingh vs Kishorilal on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18000650/
2 the offending vehicle) are directed to pay the compensation jointly and severally to the claimants.
The Insurance Company remains exonerated from any liability in this matter.
No order as to costs.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
